added: #*[[Make Chocolate Frosting|Make a chocolate frosting]] to coat your cake in for a rich dessert, or [[Make Buttercream Frosting|whip up a vanilla buttercream]] to complement the decadent chocolate cake.
#*To help traditional American buttercream stick to a cake, whip it and make it smooth.<ref>[v162092_b01]. 11 March 2022.</ref>
#*Start with room temperature butter. Otherwise, the buttercream may be stiff. It may be hard to put it on the cake. It will fall from one place to another.<ref>[v162092_b01]. 11 March 2022.</ref>

#*Put the buttercream in a warm place. Take a big pot with some hot water and set the buttercream on top of it to melt the butter slightly. The consistency of the buttercream should be light and fluffy. If the buttercream is stiff, it will not stick and look chunky. It will not be shiny.<ref>[v162092_b01]. 11 March 2022.</ref>

added: #Gather your ingredients. Pound cake is one of the simplest cakes to bake.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#[[Preheat an Oven|Preheat the oven]] to {{convert|325|F}} and grease and flour a cake pan. Pound cakes are best baked in deep pans, such as loaf pans or bundt pans. Use [[Make Butter|butter]] or shortening to grease the pan. Then, sprinkle a light layer of flour into the pan, rotate the pan until it's evenly coated, then tap out the excess flour.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 2 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#[[Cream Butter|Cream]] the butter and sugar. Place the butter and sugar in a mixing bowl and beat them together until the mixture is light, fluffy and creamy.https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 3 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 3-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 3 Version 3.jpg}}

#Add the eggs and vanilla. For best results, add the eggs one at a time and beat the mixture in between.https://www.cooksillustrated.com/how_tos/5448-adding-eggs-one-at-a-time Keep beating the mixture until the eggs are completely incorporated.https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 4 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 4-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 4 Version 3.jpg}}

#Stir in the cake flour. Keep the electric mixer on low or use a wooden spoon to stir the flour in a bit at a time until it's just incorporated. Be careful not to overmix it.https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 5 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 5-preview.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 5 Version 3.jpg}}

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the bowl.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for 1 hour 15 minutes. Rotate the pan 180 degrees halfway through the cook time to ensure it bakes evenly. The cake is finished when a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Enjoy your delicious homemade cake!<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 7 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Preheat the oven to {{convert|340|F}} and grease and flour the cake pan. You can use a round standard cake pan, a square baking dish, a loaf pan, a bundt cake pan, or whatever you have on hand. Make sure to grease it well with butter or margarine so the cake won't stick to the pan when it's baked. After you grease the pan, add a light, even layer of flour to it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 9 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Mix the wet ingredients in a large bowl. Place the butter, eggs, vanilla extract, sugar, and [[Make Buttermilk from Milk|buttermilk]] in a bowl. Use a hand or stand mixer to blend the ingredients well.https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 10 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 10-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 10 Version 3.jpg}}

#Mix the dry ingredients in a separate bowl. Sift the flour, salt, cocoa powder, and baking powder in a small bowl.https://sallysbakingaddiction.com/2016/02/24/14-kitchen-tools-every-baker-needs/ Stir them together until they are well incorporated.https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 11 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 11-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 11 Version 3.jpg}}

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture slowly. Beat the mixture on low until the batter comes together and no white bits of flour remain.https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 12 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 12-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 12 Version 3.jpg}}

#Pour the batter into the cake pan. Use a spoon or spatula to scrape the sides of the bowl so every bit of batter makes it into the pan.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 13 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Put the pan in the oven and bake the cake for 30 minutes. You may want to put the cake pan on a baking sheet in case any of the batter spills over. Rotate the cake 180 degrees halfway through the bake time to ensure it cooks evenly. The cake is ready when a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out clean, rather than coated with batter.https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 14 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 14-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 14 Version 2.jpg}}

#Take the cake from the oven and let it cool. Set it on a cooling rack and let it cool for about 5 minutes before handling it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 15 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Invert the cake onto a plate. Use whatever plate you're planning on using to serve the cake.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 16 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Let the cake cool completely before frosting it. If you try to add [[Make Frosting|frosting]] to the cake while it's still warm, the frosting will melt and run off the sides. Make some [[Make Chocolate Frosting|chocolate buttercream frosting]] or plain [[Make Buttercream Frosting|buttercream frosting]], or any other kind of frosting. Enjoy!<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 17 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Grease and flour the cake pan, then preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}}. For this recipe you should use an {{convert|8|in|cm|abbr=on}} springform pan, which has removable sides and is nice if you're serving the cake at a party. Use margarine or butter to grease the pan before flouring it to prevent the cake from sticking.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 19 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#[[Melt Butter|Melt the butter]] and allow it to cool. You can melt the butter in the microwave or on the stovetop. Let it come to room temperature before you incorporate it with the other ingredients.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 20 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Stir the dry ingredients in a small bowl. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder into a bowl and whisk them together.https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 21 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 21-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 21 Version 2.jpg}}

#Prepare the apples. Use a knife or a vegetable peeler to peel the apples, then [[Core Apples|remove their cores]]. Slice the apples into bite-sized chunks (about {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} cubes).https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 22 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 22-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 22 Version 2.jpg}}

#Blend the wet ingredients. Use a hand or stand mixer to cream the sugar and butter. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing the batter in between. Then, incorporate the vanilla into the batter.https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 23 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 23-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 23 Version 2.jpg}}

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture. You can do this by hand or use an electric mixer. Stir until the batter is smooth and creamy.https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 24 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 24-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 24 Version 2.jpg}}

#Fold in the apples. Use a spatula to gently incorporate the apples into the batter. Don't over mix the batter, since this will lead to a dense, stiff cake.https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 25 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 25-preview.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 25 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use the spatula to smooth the top of the batter so it's even.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 26 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for about 50 minutes. Put the cake pan on a baking sheet to keep your oven clean in case of spills. Rotate the cake pan 180 degrees after 25 minutes. The cake is ready when the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean.https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 27 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 27-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 27 Version 2.jpg}}

#Start by reading the ingredient list and directions before you begin. It's important to have every ingredient you need ready to go. You don't want to be running to the grocery store during preparation. The final product can flop if a key ingredient is left out.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 28 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Prepare your [[Fix a Baked Cake Stuck to the Pan|cake pans]]. Be sure to have the correct size or shape of the pan. Bundt cakes require bundt pans, while others can be baked in a variety of sizes. Grease the pans to keep the cake from sticking to them. Use about 1/2 Tbsp (7 g) of butter, margarine, or vegetable shortening on a paper towel and rub the inside of the pan. Sprinkle about 1-2 Tbsp (8-16 g) of [[Make Flour|flour]] on top.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 29 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Preheat the oven to the required temperature from the recipe. Be sure to follow the recipe, as turning the temperature higher or lower could create issues.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 30 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#[[Use Measuring Spoons and Cups|Measure ingredients]] as accurately as possible and add them in the order specified. Most cake recipes begin combining wet ingredients (like eggs, oil, and milk), then adding the dry ingredients (such as flour, baking powder, cocoa). Be sure to take special prerequisites such as [[Sift Flour|sifting]], [[Whisk Eggs|whisking]] or beating, and packing before adding the ingredients to the main bowl.

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 31 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 31-preview.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 31 Version 2.jpg}}

#Mix the cake batter as specified on the recipe. Some recipes can be mixed with a stand or hand mixer. Be cautious as steps can instruct to fold in flour or other ingredients with a rubber spatula. While mixing, stop occasionally to scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula or spoon to ensure that everything is mixed thoroughly.

{{whvid|Bake a Cake Step 32 Version 2.360p.mp4|Bake a Cake Step 32-preview Version 2.jpg|Bake a Cake Step 32 Version 2.jpg}}

#Pour the batter evenly into the prepared pans. Fill the pans two-thirds of the way full, as the cake will rise during baking. Gently tap the cake pan on the countertop to release any large air bubbles in the batter.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 33 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Place the pans on the center rack of the preheated oven. You can put the cake pan on top of a baking sheet in case any of the batter bubbles over. Do not allow the pans to touch the oven wall.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 34 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Close the oven door and immediately set a timer to the specified baking time. If there's a time range, use the median or middle number (bake it for 35 minutes for a range of 34 to 36 minutes or 53 minutes for a range of 50 to 55 minutes).  Using the median will ensure that the cake won't under or overcook.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 35 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#[[Test a Cake to See if it is Done|Check for cake doneness]]. Gently insert a toothpick or wooden skewer in the center of the cake. If it comes out clean or with a few small crumbs on it, the cake is done. If not, place it back in the oven for another 3–4 minutes. Keep testing for the same amount of time until you get the correct result.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 36 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Place the pan on a wire rack to cool for 15 to 30 minutes. Run a thin spatula around the pan edges to loosen the sides. Place the wire rack over the top of the pan, invert it, and tap it lightly to remove the cake.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 37 Version 2.jpg|center]]

removed: There's nothing like the taste of a cake you made in your own kitchen. Baking a cake is as simple as measuring ingredients, mixing them in the right order, and remembering to take the cake out of the oven before it burns. Read on to learn how to bake 3 basic cakes: vanilla pound cake, chocolate cake, and apple cake.

#Gather your ingredients. Pound cake is one of the simplest cakes to bake. Here's what you'll need:<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 24.jpg|center]]
#*1 cup (225 g) of unsalted butter, softened

#*2 cups (240 g) of cake flour (or, you can use 2 cups minus 2 Tbsp (234 g) of all-purpose flour plus 2 Tbsp (16 g) of cornstarch)<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/the-easy-way-to-make-cake-flour-substitute-baking-tips-from-the-kitchn-44521</ref>

#Preheat the oven to {{convert|325|F}} and grease and flour a cake pan. Pound cakes are best baked in deep pans, such as loaf pans or bundt pans. Use butter or shortening to grease the pan. Then, sprinkle a light layer of flour into the pan, rotate the pan until it’s evenly coated, then tap out the excess flour.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 26.jpg|center]]

#Cream the butter and sugar. Place the butter and sugar in a mixing bowl and beat them together until the mixture is light, fluffy and creamy.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 27.jpg|center]]

#Add the eggs and vanilla. For best results, add the eggs one at a time and beat the mixture in between.<ref>https://www.cooksillustrated.com/how_tos/5448-adding-eggs-one-at-a-time</ref> Keep beating the mixture until the eggs are completely incorporated.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 28.jpg|center]]

#Stir in the cake flour. Keep the electric mixer on low or use a wooden spoon to stir the flour in a bit at a time until it's just incorporated. Be careful not to overmix it.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 29.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the bowl.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 30.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for 1 hour 15 minutes. Rotate the pan 180 degrees halfway through the cook time to ensure it bakes evenly. The cake is finished when a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Enjoy your delicious homemade cake!<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 31.jpg|center]]
#Gather your ingredients. For this delicious chocolate cake, you’ll need:<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*3/4 cup (170 g) of unsalted butter, softened
#*3/4 cup (64 g) of unsweetened cocoa powder

#Preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}} and grease and flour the cake pan. You can use a round standard cake pan, a square baking dish, a loaf pan, a bundt cake pan, or whatever you have on hand. Make sure to grease it well with butter or margarine so the cake won't stick to the pan when it's baked. After you grease the pan, add a light, even layer of flour to it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 3 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Mix the wet ingredients in a large bowl. Place the butter, eggs, vanilla extract, sugar, and buttermilk in a bowl. Use a hand or stand mixer to blend the ingredients well.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*The "wet ingredients" in cake recipes are generally those that have moisture. Sugar is often listed as a wet ingredient, too, even though it isn't actually wet.
#*The wet ingredients are usually mixed first in a large bowl. The dry ingredients are mixed separately and added later.

#*It's important to follow instructions regarding the texture of the butter in cake recipes. If you use melted butter where softened butter is called for, the cake could come out flat.<ref>https://oureverydaylife.com/softened-vs-melted-butter-baking-41737.html</ref> In this case the recipe calls for softened butter. You can plan ahead by setting the butter out while you get the rest of the ingredients ready, so it has time to come to room temperature.

#Mix the dry ingredients in a separate bowl. Sift the flour, salt, cocoa powder, and baking powder in a small bowl.<ref>https://sallysbakingaddiction.com/2016/02/24/14-kitchen-tools-every-baker-needs/</ref> Stir them together until they are well incorporated.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 5 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture slowly. Beat the mixture on low until the batter comes together and no white bits of flour remain.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 6 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter into the cake pan. Use a spoon or spatula to scrape the sides of the bowl so every bit of batter makes it into the pan.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 7 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Put the pan in the oven and bake the cake for 30 minutes. You may want to put the cake pan on a baking sheet in case any of the batter spills over. Rotate the cake 180 degrees halfway through the bake time to ensure it cooks evenly. The cake is ready when a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out clean, rather than coated with batter.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 8 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#*Check the cake's progress every so often to make sure it doesn't burn. However, you should do this through the oven window instead of opening the oven door, which reduces the temperature inside the oven and can increase the bake time.

#Take the cake from the oven and let it cool. Set it on a cooling rack and let it cool for about 5 minutes before handling it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 9 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Invert the cake onto a plate. Use whatever plate you're planning on using to serve the cake.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Let the cake cool completely before frosting it. If you try to add frosting to the cake while it's still warm, the frosting will melt and run off the sides. Make some [[Make Chocolate Buttercream Icing (Frosting)|chocolate buttercream frosting]] or [[Make Buttercream Frosting|plain buttercream frosting]], or any other kind of [[Make Frosting|frosting]]. Enjoy!<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Gather your ingredients. Here's what you'll need for apple cake:<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Grease and flour the cake pan, then preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}}. For this recipe you should use an {{convert|8|in|cm|abbr=on}} springform pan, which has removable sides and is nice if you're serving the cake at a party. Use margarine or butter to grease the pan before flouring it to prevent the cake from sticking.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Melt the butter and allow it to cool. You can melt the butter in the microwave or on the stovetop. Let it come to room temperature before you incorporate it with the other ingredients.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 15.jpg|center]]

#Stir the dry ingredients in a small bowl. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder into a bowl and whisk them together.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 16.jpg|center]]

#Prepare the apples. Use a knife or a vegetable peeler to peel the apples, then remove their cores. Slice the apples into bite-sized chunks (about {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} cubes).<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 17.jpg|center]]

#Blend the wet ingredients. Use a hand or stand mixer to cream the sugar and butter. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing the batter in between. Then, incorporate the vanilla into the batter.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 18.jpg|center]]

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture. You can do this by hand or use an electric mixer. Stir until the batter is smooth and creamy.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 19.jpg|center]]

#Fold in the apples. Use a spatula to gently incorporate the apples into the batter. Don't over mix the batter, since this will lead to a dense, stiff cake.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 20.jpg|center]]
#*To keep the apples from sinking to the bottom of the bowl, toss them in flour before adding them to the batter.<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/baking-tip-toss-fruits-in-flou-84164</ref>

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use the spatula to smooth the top of the batter so it's even.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 21.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for about 50 minutes. Put the cake pan on a baking sheet to keep your oven clean in case of spills. Rotate the cake pan 180 degrees after 25 minutes. The cake is ready when the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 22.jpg|center]]
#*Serve the cake with [[Make Whipped Cream | whipped cream]], if desired.<ref>http://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/Marie-Helenes-Apple-Cake-361150</ref>

#Start by reading the ingredient list and directions before you begin. It's important to have every ingredient you need ready to go. You don't want to be running to the grocery store during preparation. The final product can flop if a key ingredient is left out.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 32.jpg|center]]

#Prepare your [[Fix a Baked Cake Stuck to the Pan|cake pans]]. Be sure to have the correct size or shape of the pan. [[Make a Strawberry Bundt Cake|Bundt cakes]] require bundt pans, while others can be baked in a variety of sizes. Grease the pans to keep the cake from sticking to them. Use about 1/2 Tbsp (7 g) of [[Make Butter|butter]], margarine, or vegetable shortening on a paper towel and rub the inside of the pan. Sprinkle about 1-2 Tbsp (8-16 g) of [[Make Flour|flour]] on top.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 33.jpg|center]]
#*Add a little flour to the pan, rotate it to ensure it adheres evenly, then shake and dump out any excess flour and set the pans to the side.

#[[Preheat an Oven|Preheat the oven]] to the required temperature from the recipe. Be sure to follow the recipe, as turning the temperature higher or lower could create issues.[[Image:325 1.jpg|center|415px]]

#[[Use Measuring Spoons and Cups|Measure ingredients]] as accurately as possible and add them in the order specified. Most cake recipes begin combining wet ingredients (like eggs, oil, and milk), then adding the dry ingredients (such as flour, baking powder, cocoa). Be sure to take special prerequisites such as [[Sift Flour|sifting]], [[Whisk Eggs|whisking]] or beating, and packing before adding the ingredients to the main bowl.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 35.jpg|center]]

#Mix the cake batter as specified on the recipe. Some recipes can be mixed with a stand or [[Remove Stuck Beaters on a Mixer|hand mixer]]. Be cautious as steps can instruct to fold in flour or other ingredients with a rubber spatula. While mixing, stop occasionally to scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula or spoon to ensure that everything is mixed thoroughly.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 36.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter evenly into the prepared pans. Fill the pans two-thirds of the way full, as the cake will rise during baking. Gently tap the cake pan on the countertop to release any large air bubbles in the batter.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 37.jpg|center]]

#Place the pans on the center rack of the preheated oven. You can put the cake pan on top of a baking sheet in case any of the batter bubbles over. Do not allow the pans to touch the oven wall.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 38.jpg|center]]

#Close the oven door and immediately set a timer to the specified baking time. If there's a time range, use the median or middle number (bake it for 35 minutes for a range of 34 to 36 minutes or 53 minutes for a range of 50 to 55 minutes).  Using the median will ensure that the cake won't under or overcook.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 39.jpg|center]]
#*Resist the urge to open the oven door during baking, as the heat will escape and may cause the cake to cook unevenly. If applicable, turn the oven light on and view through the oven window.

#[[Test a Cake to See if it is Done|Check for cake doneness]]. Gently insert a toothpick or wooden skewer in the center of the cake. If it comes out clean or with a few small crumbs on it, the cake is done. If not, place it back in the oven for another 3-4 minutes. Keep testing for the same amount of time until you get the correct result.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 40.jpg|center]]

#Place the pan on a wire rack to cool for 15 to 30 minutes. Run a thin spatula around the pan edges to loosen the sides. Place the wire rack over the top of the pan, invert it, and tap it lightly to remove the cake.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 41.jpg|center]]
#*Let it cool completely before decorating since the heat will melt frosting and icing. [[Frost a Cake|Frost]] and [[Decorate a Cake|decorate]] as desired.
*Double check your measurements before adding them to mixing bowls. A few tablespoons of missing or extra flour can have dramatic and undesired effects on the finished cake.
* Do not ice the cake before it cools. This can cause the cake to crumble and the frosting to run to the sides or slide off the cake.

*When recipes calls for cold ingredients such as butter or cream cheese to be at room temperature, unwrap the item and leave it in a bowl on the counter for 30-60 minutes to soften. You can test the softness by poking a fork or your finger in it.
* Make it vegan: substitute vegetable oil or melted coconut oil for butter.  Substitute applesauce for eggs, for instance use {{convert|1/4|cup|mL}} of applesauce in place of 1 egg.
* Use a toothpick to see if it’s fully cooked.
* Always make sure the cake pan is well buttered.
*Use high-quality, heavy duty-aluminum baking pans for even heating and best results.
*If you attempt to remove a hot cake from the pan, it may crack and fall apart.
*If you're using a different recipe, follow the directions you find in it.
*Oven temperatures vary, so keep a close eye on your cake to make sure it doesn't over-bake.
*Always wear oven mitts or protective gloves when retrieving the cake from the oven to avoid burns.
*Be sure to keep small children and pets out of the way when opening a hot oven.
*[[Make a Cake Using a Pressure Cooker]]

For this recipe you should use an {{convert|8|in|cm|abbr=on}} springform pan, which has removable sides and is nice if you're serving the cake at a party. #Stir the dry ingredients in a small bowl. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder into a bowl and whisk them together.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 16.jpg|center]]

* Always make sure the cake pan is well buttered.
*Oven temperatures vary, so keep a close eye on your cake to make sure it doesn't over-bake.
*Always wear oven mitts or protective gloves when retrieving the cake from the oven to avoid burns.
*Be sure to keep small children and pets out of the way when opening a hot oven.

#*3/4 cup (170 g) of unsalted butter, softened
#*3/4 cup (64 g) of unsweetened cocoa powder

#Preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}} and grease and flour the cake pan. You can use a round standard cake pan, a square baking dish, a loaf pan, a bundt cake pan, or whatever you have on hand. Make sure to grease it well with butter or margarine so the cake won't stick to the pan when it's baked. After you grease the pan, add a light, even layer of flour to it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 3 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Mix the wet ingredients in a large bowl. Place the butter, eggs, vanilla extract, sugar, and buttermilk in a bowl. Use a hand or stand mixer to blend the ingredients well.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*The "wet ingredients" in cake recipes are generally those that have moisture. Sugar is often listed as a wet ingredient, too, even though it isn't actually wet.
#*The wet ingredients are usually mixed first in a large bowl. The dry ingredients are mixed separately and added later.

#*It's important to follow instructions regarding the texture of the butter in cake recipes. If you use melted butter where softened butter is called for, the cake could come out flat.<ref>https://oureverydaylife.com/softened-vs-melted-butter-baking-41737.html</ref> In this case the recipe calls for softened butter. You can plan ahead by setting the butter out while you get the rest of the ingredients ready, so it has time to come to room temperature.

#Mix the dry ingredients in a separate bowl. Sift the flour, salt, cocoa powder, and baking powder in a small bowl.<ref>https://sallysbakingaddiction.com/2016/02/24/14-kitchen-tools-every-baker-needs/</ref> Stir them together until they are well incorporated.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 5 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture slowly. Beat the mixture on low until the batter comes together and no white bits of flour remain.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 6 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter into the cake pan. Use a spoon or spatula to scrape the sides of the bowl so every bit of batter makes it into the pan.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 7 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Put the pan in the oven and bake the cake for 30 minutes. You may want to put the cake pan on a baking sheet in case any of the batter spills over. Rotate the cake 180 degrees halfway through the bake time to ensure it cooks evenly. The cake is ready when a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out clean, rather than coated with batter.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 8 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#*Check the cake's progress every so often to make sure it doesn't burn. However, you should do this through the oven window instead of opening the oven door, which reduces the temperature inside the oven and can increase the bake time.

#Take the cake from the oven and let it cool. Set it on a cooling rack and let it cool for about 5 minutes before handling it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 9 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Invert the cake onto a plate. Use whatever plate you're planning on using to serve the cake.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Let the cake cool completely before frosting it. If you try to add frosting to the cake while it's still warm, the frosting will melt and run off the sides. Make some [[Make Chocolate Buttercream Icing (Frosting)|chocolate buttercream frosting]] or [[Make Buttercream Frosting|plain buttercream frosting]], or any other kind of [[Make Frosting|frosting]]. Enjoy!<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Gather your ingredients. Here's what you'll need for apple cake:<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Grease and flour the cake pan, then preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}}. For this recipe you should use an {{convert|8|in|cm|abbr=on}} springform pan, which has removable sides and is nice if you're serving the cake at a party. Use margarine or butter to grease the pan before flouring it to prevent the cake from sticking.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Melt the butter and allow it to cool. You can melt the butter in the microwave or on the stovetop. Let it come to room temperature before you incorporate it with the other ingredients.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 15.jpg|center]]

#Stir the dry ingredients in a small bowl. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder into a bowl and whisk them together.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 16.jpg|center]]

#Prepare the apples. Use a knife or a vegetable peeler to peel the apples, then remove their cores. Slice the apples into bite-sized chunks (about {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} cubes).<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 17.jpg|center]]

#Blend the wet ingredients. Use a hand or stand mixer to cream the sugar and butter. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing the batter in between. Then, incorporate the vanilla into the batter.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 18.jpg|center]]

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture. You can do this by hand or use an electric mixer. Stir until the batter is smooth and creamy.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 19.jpg|center]]

#Fold in the apples. Use a spatula to gently incorporate the apples into the batter. Don't over mix the batter, since this will lead to a dense, stiff cake.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 20.jpg|center]]
#*To keep the apples from sinking to the bottom of the bowl, toss them in flour before adding them to the batter.<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/baking-tip-toss-fruits-in-flou-84164</ref>

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use the spatula to smooth the top of the batter so it's even.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 21.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for about 50 minutes. Put the cake pan on a baking sheet to keep your oven clean in case of spills. Rotate the cake pan 180 degrees after 25 minutes. The cake is ready when the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 22.jpg|center]]
#*Serve the cake with [[Make Whipped Cream | whipped cream]], if desired.<ref>http://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/Marie-Helenes-Apple-Cake-361150</ref>

#Start by reading the ingredient list and directions before you begin. It's important to have every ingredient you need ready to go. You don't want to be running to the grocery store during preparation. The final product can flop if a key ingredient is left out.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 32.jpg|center]]

#Prepare your [[Fix a Baked Cake Stuck to the Pan|cake pans]]. Be sure to have the correct size or shape of the pan. [[Make a Strawberry Bundt Cake|Bundt cakes]] require bundt pans, while others can be baked in a variety of sizes. Grease the pans to keep the cake from sticking to them. Use about 1/2 Tbsp (7 g) of [[Make Butter|butter]], margarine, or vegetable shortening on a paper towel and rub the inside of the pan. Sprinkle about 1-2 Tbsp (8-16 g) of [[Make Flour|flour]] on top.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 33.jpg|center]]
#*Add a little flour to the pan, rotate it to ensure it adheres evenly, then shake and dump out any excess flour and set the pans to the side.

#[[Preheat an Oven|Preheat the oven]] to the required temperature from the recipe. Be sure to follow the recipe, as turning the temperature higher or lower could create issues.[[Image:325 1.jpg|center|415px]]

#[[Use Measuring Spoons and Cups|Measure ingredients]] as accurately as possible and add them in the order specified. Most cake recipes begin combining wet ingredients (like eggs, oil, and milk), then adding the dry ingredients (such as flour, baking powder, cocoa). Be sure to take special prerequisites such as [[Sift Flour|sifting]], [[Whisk Eggs|whisking]] or beating, and packing before adding the ingredients to the main bowl.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 35.jpg|center]]

#Mix the cake batter as specified on the recipe. Some recipes can be mixed with a stand or [[Remove Stuck Beaters on a Mixer|hand mixer]]. Be cautious as steps can instruct to fold in flour or other ingredients with a rubber spatula. While mixing, stop occasionally to scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula or spoon to ensure that everything is mixed thoroughly.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 36.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter evenly into the prepared pans. Fill the pans two-thirds of the way full, as the cake will rise during baking. Gently tap the cake pan on the countertop to release any large air bubbles in the batter.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 37.jpg|center]]

#Place the pans on the center rack of the preheated oven. You can put the cake pan on top of a baking sheet in case any of the batter bubbles over. Do not allow the pans to touch the oven wall.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 38.jpg|center]]

#Close the oven door and immediately set a timer to the specified baking time. If there's a time range, use the median or middle number (bake it for 35 minutes for a range of 34 to 36 minutes or 53 minutes for a range of 50 to 55 minutes).  Using the median will ensure that the cake won't under or overcook.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 39.jpg|center]]
#*Resist the urge to open the oven door during baking, as the heat will escape and may cause the cake to cook unevenly. If applicable, turn the oven light on and view through the oven window.

#[[Test a Cake to See if it is Done|Check for cake doneness]]. Gently insert a toothpick or wooden skewer in the center of the cake. If it comes out clean or with a few small crumbs on it, the cake is done. If not, place it back in the oven for another 3-4 minutes. Keep testing for the same amount of time until you get the correct result.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 40.jpg|center]]

#Place the pan on a wire rack to cool for 15 to 30 minutes. Run a thin spatula around the pan edges to loosen the sides. Place the wire rack over the top of the pan, invert it, and tap it lightly to remove the cake.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 41.jpg|center]]
#*Let it cool completely before decorating since the heat will melt frosting and icing. [[Frost a Cake|Frost]] and [[Decorate a Cake|decorate]] as desired.
*Double check your measurements before adding them to mixing bowls. A few tablespoons of missing or extra flour can have dramatic and undesired effects on the finished cake.
* Do not ice the cake before it cools. This can cause the cake to crumble and the frosting to run to the sides or slide off the cake.

*When recipes calls for cold ingredients such as butter or cream cheese to be at room temperature, unwrap the item and leave it in a bowl on the counter for 30-60 minutes to soften. You can test the softness by poking a fork or your finger in it.
* Use a toothpick to see if it’s fully cooked.
*If you attempt to remove a hot cake from the pan, it may crack and fall apart.
*If you're using a different recipe, follow the directions you find in it.
* Make it vegan: substitute vegetable oil or melted coconut oil for butter.  Substitute applesauce for eggs, for instance use {{convert|1/4|cup|mL}} of applesauce in place of 1 egg.
*Use high-quality, heavy duty-aluminum baking pans for even heating and best results.
*Oven temperatures vary, so keep a close eye on your cake to make sure it doesn't over-bake.
*Always wear oven mitts or protective gloves when retrieving the cake from the oven to avoid burns.
*Be sure to keep small children and pets out of the way when opening a hot oven.
*[[Make a Cake Using a Pressure Cooker]]

You don't want to be running to the grocery store during preparation. The final product can flop if a key ingredient is left out.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 32.jpg|center]]

#Prepare your [[Fix a Baked Cake Stuck to the Pan|cake pans]]. Be sure to have the correct size or shape of the pan. [[Make a Strawberry Bundt Cake|Bundt cakes]] require bundt pans, while others can be baked in a variety of sizes. Grease the pans to keep the cake from sticking to them. Use about 1/2 Tbsp (7 g) of [[Make Butter|butter]], margarine, or vegetable shortening on a paper towel and rub the inside of the pan. Sprinkle about 1-2 Tbsp (8-16 g) of [[Make Flour|flour]] on top.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 33.jpg|center]]
#*Add a little flour to the pan, rotate it to ensure it adheres evenly, then shake and dump out any excess flour and set the pans to the side.

#[[Preheat an Oven|Preheat the oven]] to the required temperature from the recipe. Be sure to follow the recipe, as turning the temperature higher or lower could create issues.[[Image:325 1.jpg|center|415px]]

#[[Use Measuring Spoons and Cups|Measure ingredients]] as accurately as possible and add them in the order specified. Most cake recipes begin combining wet ingredients (like eggs, oil, and milk), then adding the dry ingredients (such as flour, baking powder, cocoa). Be sure to take special prerequisites such as [[Sift Flour|sifting]], [[Whisk Eggs|whisking]] or beating, and packing before adding the ingredients to the main bowl.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 35.jpg|center]]

#Mix the cake batter as specified on the recipe. Some recipes can be mixed with a stand or [[Remove Stuck Beaters on a Mixer|hand mixer]]. Be cautious as steps can instruct to fold in flour or other ingredients with a rubber spatula. While mixing, stop occasionally to scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula or spoon to ensure that everything is mixed thoroughly.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 36.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter evenly into the prepared pans. Fill the pans two-thirds of the way full, as the cake will rise during baking. Gently tap the cake pan on the countertop to release any large air bubbles in the batter.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 37.jpg|center]]

#Place the pans on the center rack of the preheated oven. You can put the cake pan on top of a baking sheet in case any of the batter bubbles over. Do not allow the pans to touch the oven wall.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 38.jpg|center]]

#Close the oven door and immediately set a timer to the specified baking time. If there's a time range, use the median or middle number (bake it for 35 minutes for a range of 34 to 36 minutes or 53 minutes for a range of 50 to 55 minutes).  Using the median will ensure that the cake won't under or overcook.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 39.jpg|center]]
#*Resist the urge to open the oven door during baking, as the heat will escape and may cause the cake to cook unevenly. If applicable, turn the oven light on and view through the oven window.

#[[Test a Cake to See if it is Done|Check for cake doneness]]. Gently insert a toothpick or wooden skewer in the center of the cake. If it comes out clean or with a few small crumbs on it, the cake is done. If not, place it back in the oven for another 3-4 minutes. Keep testing for the same amount of time until you get the correct result.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 40.jpg|center]]

#Place the pan on a wire rack to cool for 15 to 30 minutes. Run a thin spatula around the pan edges to loosen the sides. Place the wire rack over the top of the pan, invert it, and tap it lightly to remove the cake.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 41.jpg|center]]
#*Let it cool completely before decorating since the heat will melt frosting and icing. [[Frost a Cake|Frost]] and [[Decorate a Cake|decorate]] as desired.
*Double check your measurements before adding them to mixing bowls. A few tablespoons of missing or extra flour can have dramatic and undesired effects on the finished cake.
* Do not ice the cake before it cools. This can cause the cake to crumble and the frosting to run to the sides or slide off the cake.

*When recipes calls for cold ingredients such as butter or cream cheese to be at room temperature, unwrap the item and leave it in a bowl on the counter for 30-60 minutes to soften. You can test the softness by poking a fork or your finger in it.
* Use a toothpick to see if it’s fully cooked.
*If you attempt to remove a hot cake from the pan, it may crack and fall apart.
*If you're using a different recipe, follow the directions you find in it.
* Make it vegan: substitute vegetable oil or melted coconut oil for butter.  Substitute applesauce for eggs, for instance use {{convert|1/4|cup|mL}} of applesauce in place of 1 egg.
*Use high-quality, heavy duty-aluminum baking pans for even heating and best results.
*Oven temperatures vary, so keep a close eye on your cake to make sure it doesn't over-bake.
*Always wear oven mitts or protective gloves when retrieving the cake from the oven to avoid burns.
*Be sure to keep small children and pets out of the way when opening a hot oven.
*[[Make a Cake Using a Pressure Cooker]]

Use margarine or butter to grease the pan before flouring it to prevent the cake from sticking.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Melt the butter and allow it to cool. You can melt the butter in the microwave or on the stovetop. Let it come to room temperature before you incorporate it with the other ingredients.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 15.jpg|center]]

#Stir the dry ingredients in a small bowl. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder into a bowl and whisk them together.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 16.jpg|center]]

#Prepare the apples. Use a knife or a vegetable peeler to peel the apples, then remove their cores. Slice the apples into bite-sized chunks (about {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} cubes).<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 17.jpg|center]]

#Blend the wet ingredients. Use a hand or stand mixer to cream the sugar and butter. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing the batter in between. Then, incorporate the vanilla into the batter.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 18.jpg|center]]

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture. You can do this by hand or use an electric mixer. Stir until the batter is smooth and creamy.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 19.jpg|center]]

#Fold in the apples. Use a spatula to gently incorporate the apples into the batter. Don't over mix the batter, since this will lead to a dense, stiff cake.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 20.jpg|center]]
#*To keep the apples from sinking to the bottom of the bowl, toss them in flour before adding them to the batter.<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/baking-tip-toss-fruits-in-flou-84164</ref>

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use the spatula to smooth the top of the batter so it's even.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 21.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for about 50 minutes. Put the cake pan on a baking sheet to keep your oven clean in case of spills. Rotate the cake pan 180 degrees after 25 minutes. The cake is ready when the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 22.jpg|center]]
#*Serve the cake with [[Make Whipped Cream | whipped cream]], if desired.<ref>http://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/Marie-Helenes-Apple-Cake-361150</ref>

#Start by reading the ingredient list and directions before you begin. It's important to have every ingredient you need ready to go. You don't want to be running to the grocery store during preparation. The final product can flop if a key ingredient is left out.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 32.jpg|center]]

#Prepare your [[Fix a Baked Cake Stuck to the Pan|cake pans]]. Be sure to have the correct size or shape of the pan. [[Make a Strawberry Bundt Cake|Bundt cakes]] require bundt pans, while others can be baked in a variety of sizes. Grease the pans to keep the cake from sticking to them. Use about 1/2 Tbsp (7 g) of [[Make Butter|butter]], margarine, or vegetable shortening on a paper towel and rub the inside of the pan. Sprinkle about 1-2 Tbsp (8-16 g) of [[Make Flour|flour]] on top.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 33.jpg|center]]
#*Add a little flour to the pan, rotate it to ensure it adheres evenly, then shake and dump out any excess flour and set the pans to the side.

#[[Preheat an Oven|Preheat the oven]] to the required temperature from the recipe. Be sure to follow the recipe, as turning the temperature higher or lower could create issues.[[Image:325 1.jpg|center|415px]]

#[[Use Measuring Spoons and Cups|Measure ingredients]] as accurately as possible and add them in the order specified. Most cake recipes begin combining wet ingredients (like eggs, oil, and milk), then adding the dry ingredients (such as flour, baking powder, cocoa). Be sure to take special prerequisites such as [[Sift Flour|sifting]], [[Whisk Eggs|whisking]] or beating, and packing before adding the ingredients to the main bowl.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 35.jpg|center]]

#Mix the cake batter as specified on the recipe. Some recipes can be mixed with a stand or [[Remove Stuck Beaters on a Mixer|hand mixer]]. Be cautious as steps can instruct to fold in flour or other ingredients with a rubber spatula. While mixing, stop occasionally to scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula or spoon to ensure that everything is mixed thoroughly.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 36.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter evenly into the prepared pans. Fill the pans two-thirds of the way full, as the cake will rise during baking. Gently tap the cake pan on the countertop to release any large air bubbles in the batter.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 37.jpg|center]]

#Place the pans on the center rack of the preheated oven. You can put the cake pan on top of a baking sheet in case any of the batter bubbles over. Do not allow the pans to touch the oven wall.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 38.jpg|center]]

#Close the oven door and immediately set a timer to the specified baking time. If there's a time range, use the median or middle number (bake it for 35 minutes for a range of 34 to 36 minutes or 53 minutes for a range of 50 to 55 minutes).  Using the median will ensure that the cake won't under or overcook.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 39.jpg|center]]
#*Resist the urge to open the oven door during baking, as the heat will escape and may cause the cake to cook unevenly. If applicable, turn the oven light on and view through the oven window.

#[[Test a Cake to See if it is Done|Check for cake doneness]]. Gently insert a toothpick or wooden skewer in the center of the cake. If it comes out clean or with a few small crumbs on it, the cake is done. If not, place it back in the oven for another 3-4 minutes. Keep testing for the same amount of time until you get the correct result.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 40.jpg|center]]

#Place the pan on a wire rack to cool for 15 to 30 minutes. Run a thin spatula around the pan edges to loosen the sides. Place the wire rack over the top of the pan, invert it, and tap it lightly to remove the cake.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 41.jpg|center]]
#*Let it cool completely before decorating since the heat will melt frosting and icing. [[Frost a Cake|Frost]] and [[Decorate a Stunning Cake|decorate]] as desired.
*Double check your measurements before adding them to mixing bowls. A few tablespoons of missing or extra flour can have dramatic and undesired effects on the finished cake.
* Do not ice the cake before it cools. This can cause the cake to crumble and the frosting to run to the sides or slide off the cake.

*When recipes calls for cold ingredients such as butter or cream cheese to be at room temperature, unwrap the item and leave it in a bowl on the counter for 30-60 minutes to soften. You can test the softness by poking a fork or your finger in it.
* Use a toothpick to see if it’s fully cooked.
*If you attempt to remove a hot cake from the pan, it may crack and fall apart.
*If you're using a different recipe, follow the directions you find in it.
* Make it vegan: substitute vegetable oil or melted coconut oil for butter.  Substitute applesauce for eggs, for instance use {{convert|1/4|cup|mL}} of applesauce in place of 1 egg.
*Use high-quality, heavy duty-aluminum baking pans for even heating and best results.
*Oven temperatures vary, so keep a close eye on your cake to make sure it doesn't over-bake.
*Always wear oven mitts or protective gloves when retrieving the cake from the oven to avoid burns.
*Be sure to keep small children and pets out of the way when opening a hot oven.
*[[Make a Cake Using a Pressure Cooker]]

#Add the eggs and vanilla. #*The wet ingredients are usually mixed first in a large bowl. The dry ingredients are mixed separately and added later.

removed: There's nothing like the taste of a cake you made in your own kitchen. Baking a cake is as simple as measuring ingredients, mixing them in the right order, and remembering to take the cake out of the oven before it burns. Read on to learn how to bake 3 basic cakes: vanilla pound cake, chocolate cake, and apple cake.

#Gather your ingredients. Pound cake is one of the simplest cakes to bake. Here's what you'll need:<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 24.jpg|center]]
#*1 cup (225 g) of unsalted butter, softened

#*2 cups (240 g) of cake flour (or, you can use 2 cups minus 2 Tbsp (234 g) of all-purpose flour plus 2 Tbsp (16 g) of cornstarch)<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/the-easy-way-to-make-cake-flour-substitute-baking-tips-from-the-kitchn-44521</ref>

#Preheat the oven to {{convert|325|F}} and grease and flour a cake pan. Pound cakes are best baked in deep pans, such as loaf pans or bundt pans. Use butter or shortening to grease the pan. Then, sprinkle a light layer of flour into the pan, rotate the pan until it’s evenly coated, then tap out the excess flour.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 26.jpg|center]]

#Cream the butter and sugar. Place the butter and sugar in a mixing bowl and beat them together until the mixture is light, fluffy and creamy.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 27.jpg|center]]

#Add the eggs and vanilla. For best results, add the eggs one at a time and beat the mixture in between.<ref>https://www.cooksillustrated.com/how_tos/5448-adding-eggs-one-at-a-time</ref> Keep beating the mixture until the eggs are completely incorporated.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 28.jpg|center]]

#Stir in the cake flour. Keep the electric mixer on low or use a wooden spoon to stir the flour in a bit at a time until it's just incorporated. Be careful not to overmix it.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 29.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the bowl.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 30.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for 1 hour 15 minutes. Rotate the pan 180 degrees halfway through the cook time to ensure it bakes evenly. The cake is finished when a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Enjoy your delicious homemade cake!<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 31.jpg|center]]
#Gather your ingredients. For this delicious chocolate cake, you’ll need:<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*3/4 cup (170 g) of unsalted butter, softened
#*3/4 cup (64 g) of unsweetened cocoa powder

#Preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}} and grease and flour the cake pan. You can use a round standard cake pan, a square baking dish, a loaf pan, a bundt cake pan, or whatever you have on hand. Make sure to grease it well with butter or margarine so the cake won't stick to the pan when it's baked. After you grease the pan, add a light, even layer of flour to it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 3 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Mix the wet ingredients in a large bowl. Place the butter, eggs, vanilla extract, sugar, and buttermilk in a bowl. Use a hand or stand mixer to blend the ingredients well.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*The "wet ingredients" in cake recipes are generally those that have moisture. Sugar is often listed as a wet ingredient, too, even though it isn't actually wet.
#*The wet ingredients are usually mixed first in a large bowl. The dry ingredients are mixed separately and added later.

#*It's important to follow instructions regarding the texture of the butter in cake recipes. If you use melted butter where softened butter is called for, the cake could come out flat.<ref>https://oureverydaylife.com/softened-vs-melted-butter-baking-41737.html</ref> In this case the recipe calls for softened butter. You can plan ahead by setting the butter out while you get the rest of the ingredients ready, so it has time to come to room temperature.

#Mix the dry ingredients in a separate bowl. Sift the flour, salt, cocoa powder, and baking powder in a small bowl.<ref>https://sallysbakingaddiction.com/2016/02/24/14-kitchen-tools-every-baker-needs/</ref> Stir them together until they are well incorporated.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 5 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture slowly. Beat the mixture on low until the batter comes together and no white bits of flour remain.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 6 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter into the cake pan. Use a spoon or spatula to scrape the sides of the bowl so every bit of batter makes it into the pan.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 7 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Put the pan in the oven and bake the cake for 30 minutes. You may want to put the cake pan on a baking sheet in case any of the batter spills over. Rotate the cake 180 degrees halfway through the bake time to ensure it cooks evenly. The cake is ready when a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out clean, rather than coated with batter.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 8 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#*Check the cake's progress every so often to make sure it doesn't burn. However, you should do this through the oven window instead of opening the oven door, which reduces the temperature inside the oven and can increase the bake time.

#Take the cake from the oven and let it cool. Set it on a cooling rack and let it cool for about 5 minutes before handling it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 9 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Invert the cake onto a plate. Use whatever plate you're planning on using to serve the cake.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Let the cake cool completely before frosting it. If you try to add frosting to the cake while it's still warm, the frosting will melt and run off the sides. Make some [[Make Chocolate Buttercream Icing (Frosting)|chocolate buttercream frosting]] or [[Make Buttercream Frosting|plain buttercream frosting]], or any other kind of [[Make Frosting|frosting]]. Enjoy!<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Gather your ingredients. Here's what you'll need for apple cake:<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Grease and flour the cake pan, then preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}}. For this recipe you should use an {{convert|8|in|cm|abbr=on}} springform pan, which has removable sides and is nice if you're serving the cake at a party. Use margarine or butter to grease the pan before flouring it to prevent the cake from sticking.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Melt the butter and allow it to cool. You can melt the butter in the microwave or on the stovetop. Let it come to room temperature before you incorporate it with the other ingredients.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 15.jpg|center]]

#Stir the dry ingredients in a small bowl. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder into a bowl and whisk them together.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 16.jpg|center]]

#Prepare the apples. Use a knife or a vegetable peeler to peel the apples, then remove their cores. Slice the apples into bite-sized chunks (about {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} cubes).<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 17.jpg|center]]

#Blend the wet ingredients. Use a hand or stand mixer to cream the sugar and butter. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing the batter in between. Then, incorporate the vanilla into the batter.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 18.jpg|center]]

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture. You can do this by hand or use an electric mixer. Stir until the batter is smooth and creamy.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 19.jpg|center]]

#Fold in the apples. Use a spatula to gently incorporate the apples into the batter. Don't over mix the batter, since this will lead to a dense, stiff cake.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 20.jpg|center]]
#*To keep the apples from sinking to the bottom of the bowl, toss them in flour before adding them to the batter.<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/baking-tip-toss-fruits-in-flou-84164</ref>

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use the spatula to smooth the top of the batter so it's even.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 21.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for about 50 minutes. Put the cake pan on a baking sheet to keep your oven clean in case of spills. Rotate the cake pan 180 degrees after 25 minutes. The cake is ready when the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 22.jpg|center]]
#*Serve the cake with [[Make Whipped Cream | whipped cream]], if desired.<ref>http://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/Marie-Helenes-Apple-Cake-361150</ref>

#Start by reading the ingredient list and directions before you begin. It's important to have every ingredient you need ready to go. You don't want to be running to the grocery store during preparation. The final product can flop if a key ingredient is left out.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 32.jpg|center]]

#Prepare your [[Fix a Baked Cake Stuck to the Pan|cake pans]]. Be sure to have the correct size or shape of the pan. [[Make a Strawberry Bundt Cake|Bundt cakes]] require bundt pans, while others can be baked in a variety of sizes. Grease the pans to keep the cake from sticking to them. Use about 1/2 Tbsp (7 g) of [[Make Butter|butter]], margarine, or vegetable shortening on a paper towel and rub the inside of the pan. Sprinkle about 1-2 Tbsp (8-16 g) of [[Make Flour|flour]] on top.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 33.jpg|center]]
#*Add a little flour to the pan, rotate it to ensure it adheres evenly, then shake and dump out any excess flour and set the pans to the side.

#[[Preheat an Oven|Preheat the oven]] to the required temperature from the recipe. Be sure to follow the recipe, as turning the temperature higher or lower could create issues.[[Image:325 1.jpg|center|415px]]

#[[Use Measuring Spoons and Cups|Measure ingredients]] as accurately as possible and add them in the order specified. Most cake recipes begin combining wet ingredients (like eggs, oil, and milk), then adding the dry ingredients (such as flour, baking powder, cocoa). Be sure to take special prerequisites such as [[Sift Flour|sifting]], [[Whisk Eggs|whisking]] or beating, and packing before adding the ingredients to the main bowl.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 35.jpg|center]]

#Mix the cake batter as specified on the recipe. Some recipes can be mixed with a stand or [[Remove Stuck Beaters on a Mixer|hand mixer]]. Be cautious as steps can instruct to fold in flour or other ingredients with a rubber spatula. While mixing, stop occasionally to scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula or spoon to ensure that everything is mixed thoroughly.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 36.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter evenly into the prepared pans. Fill the pans two-thirds of the way full, as the cake will rise during baking. Gently tap the cake pan on the countertop to release any large air bubbles in the batter.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 37.jpg|center]]

#Place the pans on the center rack of the preheated oven. You can put the cake pan on top of a baking sheet in case any of the batter bubbles over. Do not allow the pans to touch the oven wall.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 38.jpg|center]]

#Close the oven door and immediately set a timer to the specified baking time. If there's a time range, use the median or middle number (bake it for 35 minutes for a range of 34 to 36 minutes or 53 minutes for a range of 50 to 55 minutes).  Using the median will ensure that the cake won't under or overcook.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 39.jpg|center]]
#*Resist the urge to open the oven door during baking, as the heat will escape and may cause the cake to cook unevenly. If applicable, turn the oven light on and view through the oven window.

#[[Test a Cake to See if it is Done|Check for cake doneness]]. Gently insert a toothpick or wooden skewer in the center of the cake. If it comes out clean or with a few small crumbs on it, the cake is done. If not, place it back in the oven for another 3-4 minutes. Keep testing for the same amount of time until you get the correct result.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 40.jpg|center]]

#Place the pan on a wire rack to cool for 15 to 30 minutes. Run a thin spatula around the pan edges to loosen the sides. Place the wire rack over the top of the pan, invert it, and tap it lightly to remove the cake.[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 41.jpg|center]]
#*Let it cool completely before decorating since the heat will melt frosting and icing. [[Frost a Cake|Frost]] and [[Decorate a Stunning Cake|decorate]] as desired.
*Double check your measurements before adding them to mixing bowls. A few tablespoons of missing or extra flour can have dramatic and undesired effects on the finished cake.
* Do not ice the cake before it cools. This can cause the cake to crumble and the frosting to run to the sides or slide off the cake.

*When recipes calls for cold ingredients such as butter or cream cheese to be at room temperature, unwrap the item and leave it in a bowl on the counter for 30-60 minutes to soften. You can test the softness by poking a fork or your finger in it.
* Use a toothpick to see if it’s fully cooked.
*If you attempt to remove a hot cake from the pan, it may crack and fall apart.
*If you're using a different recipe, follow the directions you find in it.
* Make it vegan: substitute vegetable oil or melted coconut oil for butter.  Substitute applesauce for eggs, for instance use {{convert|1/4|cup|mL}} of applesauce in place of 1 egg.
*Use high-quality, heavy duty-aluminum baking pans for even heating and best results.
*Be sure to keep small children and pets out of the way when opening a hot oven.
*Oven temperatures vary, so keep a close eye on your cake to make sure it doesn't over-bake.
*Always wear oven mitts or protective gloves when retrieving the cake from the oven to avoid burns.
*[[Make a Cake Using a Pressure Cooker]]

#Stir in the cake flour. Keep the electric mixer on low or use a wooden spoon to stir the flour in a bit at a time until it's just incorporated. Be careful not to overmix it.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 29.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the bowl.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 30.jpg|center]]

#Bake the cake for 1 hour 15 minutes. Rotate the pan 180 degrees halfway through the cook time to ensure it bakes evenly. The cake is finished when a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Enjoy your delicious homemade cake!<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/classic-pound-cake-353169</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 31.jpg|center]]
#Gather your ingredients. For this delicious chocolate cake, you’ll need:<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*3/4 cup (170 g) of unsalted butter, softened
#*3/4 cup (64 g) of unsweetened cocoa powder

#Preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}} and grease and flour the cake pan. You can use a round standard cake pan, a square baking dish, a loaf pan, a bundt cake pan, or whatever you have on hand. Make sure to grease it well with butter or margarine so the cake won't stick to the pan when it's baked. After you grease the pan, add a light, even layer of flour to it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 3 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Mix the wet ingredients in a large bowl. Place the butter, eggs, vanilla extract, sugar, and buttermilk in a bowl. Use a hand or stand mixer to blend the ingredients well.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 4 Version 2.jpg|center]]
#*The "wet ingredients" in cake recipes are generally those that have moisture. Sugar is often listed as a wet ingredient, too, even though it isn't actually wet.
#*The wet ingredients are usually mixed first in a large bowl. The dry ingredients are mixed separately and added later.

#*It's important to follow instructions regarding the texture of the butter in cake recipes. If you use melted butter where softened butter is called for, the cake could come out flat.<ref>https://oureverydaylife.com/softened-vs-melted-butter-baking-41737.html</ref> In this case the recipe calls for softened butter. #Put the pan in the oven and bake the cake for 30 minutes. You may want to put the cake pan on a baking sheet in case any of the batter spills over. Rotate the cake 180 degrees halfway through the bake time to ensure it cooks evenly. #Take the cake from the oven and let it cool. Set it on a cooling rack and let it cool for about 5 minutes before handling it.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 9 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Invert the cake onto a plate. Use whatever plate you're planning on using to serve the cake.<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Let the cake cool completely before frosting it. If you try to add frosting to the cake while it's still warm, the frosting will melt and run off the sides. Make some [[Make Chocolate Buttercream Icing (Frosting)|chocolate buttercream frosting]] or [[Make Buttercream Frosting|plain buttercream frosting]], or any other kind of [[Make Frosting|frosting]]. Enjoy!<ref>https://steemit.com/steemit/@mohamed1230/making-chocolate-cake</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Grease and flour the cake pan, then preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F}}. For this recipe you should use an {{convert|8|in|cm|abbr=on}} springform pan, which has removable sides and is nice if you're serving the cake at a party. Use margarine or butter to grease the pan before flouring it to prevent the cake from sticking.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 14.jpg|center]]

#Melt the butter and allow it to cool. You can melt the butter in the microwave or on the stovetop. Let it come to room temperature before you incorporate it with the other ingredients.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 15.jpg|center]]

#Stir the dry ingredients in a small bowl. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder into a bowl and whisk them together.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 16.jpg|center]]

#Prepare the apples. Use a knife or a vegetable peeler to peel the apples, then remove their cores. Slice the apples into bite-sized chunks (about {{convert|1/2|in|cm}} cubes).<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 17.jpg|center]]

#Blend the wet ingredients. Use a hand or stand mixer to cream the sugar and butter. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing the batter in between. Then, incorporate the vanilla into the batter.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 18.jpg|center]]

#Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture. You can do this by hand or use an electric mixer. Stir until the batter is smooth and creamy.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 19.jpg|center]]

#Fold in the apples. Use a spatula to gently incorporate the apples into the batter. Don't over mix the batter, since this will lead to a dense, stiff cake.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 20.jpg|center]]

#Pour the batter into the pan. Use the spatula to smooth the top of the batter so it's even.<ref>https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/marie-helenes-apple-cake-361150</ref>[[Image:Bake a Cake Step 21.jpg|center]]
